title: Adjust an ironing board to a lower working height
instruction: Lower the ironing board to its marked working height and leave it locked.
context: An adjustable domestic ironing board must be lowered without letting its loaded crossed legs collapse. One hand takes the deck's weight while the other operates the spring-return height lever.
setup: A full-size 1100 × 300 mm domestic ironing board with a pale blue cotton cover, empty steel iron rest, crossed steel-tube legs and an orange spring-return height lever stands on a level floor with its deck at 888 mm. A metal height ruler beside the board marks 805 mm in green. The two YAM arms start clear on fixed pedestals 610 mm apart.
scoring: Award 1.0 when the deck sits within 12 mm of the 805 mm mark, the returned lever and lower runner share at least 4 mm in both bearing-face directions with at most 4 mm of clearance, and the deck bears its own weight with both grippers clear for one second. At the correct height award 0.65 for an engaged catch before hands-off verification, or 0.40 if the catch is open. Score 0 at other heights.
reset_notes: Remove any iron and return the board to its higher locked working position.
fidelity: Full-size steel deck and crossed legs use passive joints and an actual bearing latch at each working height. A floor guide keeps the sliding foot in its plane while it tracks the deck slider.
scores: Demo: 1.0 in 286 actions. Dream-1: 0.0 after 380 actions.
